rationale: Search by meaning is a later setting of the one memory search that F041 switches on for each parent's agent, not a second feature: the same `memory.search.provider` key moves from keyword-only to a local embedding model on the Mac mini once the llama.cpp provider plugin is installed, F041's own caveat says its search is by keyword 'until local embeddings are added (F046)', and the chunk reviews of rounds 1 to 3 each listed F041 among F046's merge hints without a merge pass taking it up, although rounds 2 and 3 folded realtime voice into Talk and Home Assistant into house devices on this same ground (a later mode that replaces the first is not a second feature). No rule forbids it: F046's 'later' wave rests on priority (value 2) and not on a dependency or a new kind of risk, since its own correction says the text leg does not need the skipped local-model milestone, it is the lower-risk half (no tool, no send path, note text stays on the Mac mini) on the same agents, and the wave A card ships on keyword search at F041's medium risk and states the embedding step as a later step with its install and its limits (text only, a silent drop back to keyword search if the local server fails), while the shared family handbook (F043), whose search it also improves, stays its own card because it is shared between the two parents' agents.
name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' is saved to that parent's own notes and found again (by keyword first; by meaning with local embeddings as a later step)

rationale: Both are built from the same plumbing on the parent's own agent, with no new tool: a page of the children's facts (emergency contacts, allergies, medicines, conditions) in the shared family folder (F043) and a prompt rule in AGENTS.md that turns it into something the parent prints, forwards or pastes, so kept apart the same facts are entered on two pages (CRT-13's plan page and CRT-12's per-child form-facts section) and the templates go out in two separate pieces of work; the chunk reviews of rounds 2 and 3 listed CRT-13 among CRT-12's merge hints, but no merge pass proposed or ruled on the pair. No rule forbids it: CRT-12's wave C rests on no later dependency (the family folder, the household store, photo and PDF reading and reminders are all wave A), neither card lists a decision for Tony, both are medium risk with nothing filled in, signed, submitted or sent by Happy, and the wave B card states its parts separately (the emergency plan and the sitter sheet; the document index, the form due-date reminder and the paste-ready form answers; the fixed reply to emergency phrases), says that the children's health facts reach the cloud model whenever a sheet or an answer block is drafted and are never handed to the research agent, and leaves expiry dates with the renewals look-ahead (F063).
name: Family paperwork from one set of family facts: the emergency card, the sitter sheet and the school, camp and health-form kit (document index, form due dates, paste-ready answers), plus a fixed reply to emergency texts
